# docker-compose.yml: halogen-flash-server, two-container topology.
#
# ONE IMAGE, TWO ROLES. The release image's entrypoint takes `engine` or `api`
# as its argument, so both services below are the same build and cannot drift
# apart.
#
# Two services because they have nothing in common at RESTART time: the engine
# needs the GPU and re-reads the weights; the front-end needs a tokenizer and
# starts in a second. Splitting them means a front-end change redeploys without
# a model reload. If you do not need that, the single container is simpler:
#
#   podman run --rm -it --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri \
#     --group-add keep-groups --ipc=host --ulimit memlock=-1:-1 \
#     -v /path/to/halogen-models:/models:ro \
#     -p 8731:8731 ghcr.io/peonist-ai/halogen-flash-server:0.15.0
#
# ONE VOLUME IS ENOUGH. The weights repo ships the tokenizer inside it, and
# both services below read it from there. Set HALOGEN_MODELS to the directory
# `hf download` wrote and nothing else is required.
#
# The engine port is deliberately NOT published, because the token protocol has
# no auth. Only the API is reachable, and it is the only edge.
#
# `keep-groups` in group_add is a PODMAN extension, so this file is written for
# podman-compose. Under docker compose, replace it with
# `group_add: ["video", "render"]`.
#
# Usage:
#   HALOGEN_MODELS=~/halogen-models podman-compose up -d
#   podman-compose restart api          # cheap: no model reload
#   podman-compose logs -f engine       # watch the load, it takes minutes
#
# BOTH SERVICES MUST RUN THE SAME TAG. The api renders the prompt and the
# engine runs it, and what one release can do the other may not know how to
# ask for. Public issue #26 was an api at 0.4.4 in front of an engine at
# 0.5.6: the front-end predated images, so it rendered the chat template's
# image placeholder and never sent the pixels, and every picture was
# described from nothing, with no error anywhere. The api now warns at
# startup when the engine's version differs from its own, and /health shows
# both, but the fix is this file: one tag, changed in both places.
services:
  engine:
    image: ghcr.io/peonist-ai/halogen-flash-server:0.15.0
    command: ["engine"]
    environment:
      HALOGEN_CTX: "131072"
      HALOGEN_KV_POOL_POSITIONS: "131072"
      HALOGEN_KV_SLOTS: "1"
      HALOGEN_MAX_TOK: "16384"
      HALOGEN_HOST_RESERVE_GIB: "28"
      HALOGEN_CACHE_BRANCHES: "3"

      HALOGEN_MAX_TOKENS_DEFAULT: "8192"
      HALOGEN_MAX_TOKENS_CAP: "16384"

      HALOGEN_PROMPT_CACHE: "2"
      HALOGEN_COMPOSABLE_CONTEXT: "0"
      HALOGEN_WEIGHTS_LOCK: "1"
      HALOGEN_ENGINE_WATCHDOG_S: "0"
      HALOGEN_VERBOSE: "1"
      # Separate netns from the api service, so the engine must listen on all
      # interfaces WITHIN the compose network. It stays unpublished to the host.
      HALOGEN_BIND: 0.0.0.0
      # NOTHING ELSE IS SET HERE ON PURPOSE. The image already carries the
      # shipped defaults (1 KV slot, 262,144 context, prompt cache mode 2,
      # prefill chunk 32,768, the quality sidecar, the tuned GEMM plan). A copy
      # of a default in a second file is a copy that goes stale: when the image
      # changes, this file would silently override it with last release's
      # value. Override here only what you actually mean to change, and see
      # docs/FLAGS.md for what each one costs.
      #
      # The slots share one KV pool of HALOGEN_CTX positions (~26 KiB each)
      # plus ~115 MiB per slot; 4 x 262,144 is ~28 GiB and is the default.
      #
      # Contexts past the native 262,144 (up to 1,048,576) need the model's
      # static YaRN factor as well, and are a different model configuration:
      # see the README's "1M context" section before uncommenting these.
      # HALOGEN_ROPE_YARN: "4"
      # HALOGEN_CTX: "1048576"
      #
      # The attention budget: how many tokens of the context each query
      # attends through the model's sparse attention. The checkpoint's value
      # is 2048 and is the default. 4096 retrieved two more of 96 planted
      # facts at 16k in the README's battery for about 7% of prefill speed
      # at 32k and 2% of decode; it is a different model configuration, not
      # byte-identical. See the README's "Attention budget" section.
      # HALOGEN_INDEXER_BUDGET: "4096"
      #
      # IMAGES ARE OFF UNTIL THIS IS SET, and unset is the shipped state: with
      # no tower the engine never builds one, allocates nothing for it, and
      # every image path is unreachable, so a text server is byte-identical to
      # a build without any of it. Point it at the vision sidecar (0.84 GiB,
      # fetched beside the checkpoint) to accept images on
      # /v1/chat/completions and /v1/responses. `1` resolves to the sidecar
      # beside the checkpoint. An image costs about 1,000 tokens at 1280x800
      # and 2,040 at 1080p, out of the same context as the prompt.
      HALOGEN_VISION_TOWER: ${HALOGEN_VISION_TOWER:-}
      #
      # BRING YOUR OWN GGUF (0.7.0). Point this at a llama.cpp GGUF of the
      # model (any shard of a split) and the engine repacks it into RAM at
      # startup, losslessly, and serves it with its own draft head
      # (qwen38-flash-next-mtp.hgn, 1.4 GiB, beside the GGUF or from
      # HALOGEN_MTP_HEAD). The models volume then holds the GGUF, the head
      # and tokenizer/; no checkpoint, no sidecar. Startup is a read of the
      # whole file every time unless HALOGEN_GGUF_CACHE=1 keeps the repack
      # beside it (about 70 GiB, written once; needs the volume writable).
      # The README's "Bring your own GGUF" section has which files and the
      # numbers.
      # HALOGEN_CHECKPOINT: /models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-IQ4_XS-00001-of-00003.gguf
      # HALOGEN_GGUF_CACHE: "1"
      #
      # THE PROMPT CACHE ON DISK (0.10.0). Point this at a directory on a real
      # filesystem (it takes O_DIRECT; a tmpfs cannot hold it) and every
      # conversation's KV rows are written behind the request as it grows;
      # after a restart, a follow-up turn resumes from the drive instead of
      # re-prefilling the conversation. 27 KiB a token: 0.9 GB at 32k, 7.2 GB
      # at 262k. HALOGEN_CACHE_DISK_GIB (default 64) bounds the directory,
      # least recently used conversations out. See the README's "Prompt cache
      # on disk" section, and stop_grace_period below.
      # HALOGEN_CACHE_DIR: /cache
      # HALOGEN_CACHE_DISK_GIB: "64"
    volumes:
      - ~/models/halogen-qwen38-flash-next:/models:ro
      # The directory `hf download` wrote. It holds the checkpoint, the quality
      # sidecar the engine picks up automatically, and tokenizer/.
      #- ${HALOGEN_MODELS:?set HALOGEN_MODELS to the directory hf download wrote}:/models:ro
      # The prompt cache's disk tier, if HALOGEN_CACHE_DIR is set above:
      # - ${HALOGEN_CACHE:-./halogen-cache}:/cache
    devices:
      - /dev/kfd
      - /dev/dri
    # `ipc: host` is load-bearing: without it the GPU runtime dies during
    # startup, and no `shm_size` substitutes (five sizes from 64 MiB to
    # 64 GiB fail identically; the shared namespace itself is what is
    # needed). `seccomp:unconfined` used to sit beside it and was measured
    # to do nothing here (public issue #8: starts and serves without it
    # under Podman; the reporter runs Docker 29 without it), so 0.6.1
    # dropped it.
    ipc: host
    ulimits:
      memlock: -1
    group_add:
      - "44"
      - "992"
    # THE API MUST NOT START UNTIL THIS ANSWERS. Reading the weights takes
    # minutes, and `depends_on` alone waits only for the container to START.
    # Without this the front-end connects, is refused, and exits at boot:
    #   ConnectionRefusedError: [Errno 111] Connect call failed
    # then crash-loops under `restart` until the engine happens to be ready.
    # start_period is what buys the load time: failures during it do not count.
    # A CONNECT IS NOT A HEALTHCHECK. This probed `</dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/8730`,
    # which the kernel completes into the listen backlog with no help from the
    # engine: an engine whose GPU queue has aborted answers it forever.
    # Measured on 0.4.4 with the engine stopped: green healthcheck, /health
    # "ok", every request hung. halogen-healthcheck asks for a PONG, which the
    # engine answers between decode rounds and between prefill chunks, so a
    # busy server stays healthy and a wedged one does not.
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "/usr/local/bin/halogen-healthcheck", "engine"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 35s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 20m
    # A stop sends SIGTERM and, 10 s later by default, SIGKILL. The engine
    # finishes writing the last turn's rows to the disk tier on SIGTERM
    # (usually well under a second; a 262k first turn on a slow drive can
    # take longer), so give it a minute rather than lose that turn.
    stop_grace_period: 60s
    restart: "no"
    security_opt:
      - seccomp=unconfined

  api:
    image: ghcr.io/peonist-ai/halogen-flash-server:0.15.0
    command: ["api"]
    depends_on:
      engine:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      HALOGEN_ENGINE: engine:8730
    volumes:
      - ~/models/halogen-qwen38-flash-next:/models:ro
      # Read-only, and only so the front-end can find tokenizer/ in the same
      # directory. Set HALOGEN_TOKENIZER instead if your tokenizer lives
      # elsewhere; it must be a FLAT directory, because HuggingFace cache
      # snapshots are symlinks into a sibling blobs/ that dangle in a container.
      #- ${HALOGEN_MODELS:?set HALOGEN_MODELS to the directory hf download wrote}:/models:ro
    ports:
      - "8731:8731"          # the only published port
    # /health asks the ENGINE for a PONG before it answers, so this is a
    # check on the pair rather than on the front-end's own process. A live
    # front-end in front of a dead engine used to report itself healthy.
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "/usr/local/bin/halogen-healthcheck", "api"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 35s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 2m
    restart: "no"
    security_opt:
      - seccomp=unconfined

env: HALOGEN_IMAGE_MODES=all engine api bench sweep convert inspect verify ppl niah

env: HALOGEN_IMAGE_MODES=all engine api bench sweep convert inspect verify ppl niah

vision.input: data: URL or bare base64 in an image content part; http(s) URLs are refused
disabled_because: the engine was started without a vision tower (HALOGEN_VISION_TOWER)

health.decode: greedy at temperature 0 (the default); sampled at temperature > 0

prompt_lookup.applies_to: greedy requests with the mtp drafter

health.server_defaults_rule: a field the request sends always wins; a default fills only a field the request omits. A request that sends temperature 0 decodes greedy and takes no sampling default

structured_output.sampling: greedy only (temperature 0); sampled + schema is a 400
structured_output.images: a schema with images is a 400
structured_output.thinking: the reasoning block is unconstrained; the final text is constrained after </think>
structured_output.tools: a request with tools may open a <tool_call> instead of the JSON (the schema binds the final text, not a call)
structured_output.keys: object keys are emitted in schema order

sampling.decode: temperature 0 (the default) is greedy: a forward pass and an argmax, byte-identical to serial greedy decode. temperature > 0 samples from the filtered target on the same drafter the request would otherwise get; with the MTP drafter the speculative accept/reject rule emits exactly the target distribution
sampling.filters: top_k, top_p and min_p compose as an intersection (the HF/vLLM convention); top_p >= 1 and top_k = 0 disable a filter. A sampled request that omits top_k or top_p takes the operator's default, else the model's (filter_defaults)
sampling.seed: reproduces a request on the same drafter; a sampled MTP run and a sampled serial run agree in distribution, not token for token
sampling.penalties: presence and frequency count GENERATED tokens only; applied on both drafters
sampling.logprobs: a sampled request carries the chosen token's logprob on every token; at temperature 0, and with top_logprobs (up to 20) at any temperature, the first generated token only, so those need max_tokens 1
not_implemented: logprobs past the first token at temperature 0
